sentence_stem: Had she known about the storm,
correct_completion: she would have postponed the journey.
full_sentence: Had she known about the storm, she would have postponed the journey.
acceptable_variants: she would have chosen another route.
she might not have set out at all.

options.text: she sets out at dawn as planned.
options.why_wrong: The present tense does not match the unreal past set up by the inverted 'Had she known'; the result clause needs 'would have' plus a past participle.
A future form with 'will' cannot express the unreal past result of an inverted third conditional.

options.text: she would have postponed the journey.
she wanted to postpone the journey.
options.why_wrong: A simple past states a past desire or fact and does not express the hypothetical result that follows an inverted third conditional.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional with 'Had + subject' and a 'would have' result clause
explanation: After the inverted form 'Had she known', the main clause must express an unreal past result, so we need 'would have' plus a past participle. Polish speakers may find this perfect modal unfamiliar, because Polish builds the conditional from a past-tense verb plus a particle, without a separate perfect form.
translation: Gdyby wiedziała o burzy, odłożyłaby podróż.
